title: On Smiling at the oldest joke once more
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：smile　|　正文 357 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 smile 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the cook ① smiled at the oldest joke once more with great care, and every guest in the canteen said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the cook ② smiles at the oldest joke once more on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ smile at the oldest joke once more at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ smiled at the oldest joke once more before — a line in the menu for September 1978 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Smiling at the oldest joke once more with great care, the cook said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bowl at the far table, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ smile his thanks without words on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Smile his thanks without words at once and never mention it again.

By 1991 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the menu, and a new guest from the next canteen ⑧ smiles his thanks without words with great care every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the table, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ smiled at the oldest joke once more again when nobody else would.

⑩ To smile at the oldest joke once more, my mother said in 1996, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the canteen remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the canteen forgets, somebody smiles at the oldest joke once more on the same day again and somebody must smile at the oldest joke once more with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 微笑（一般过去式 smiled at the oldest joke once more：1984 年厨子头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 微笑（一般现在 smiles at the oldest joke once more：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 微笑（不定式 to smile at the oldest joke once more：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 微笑（过去完成时 had smiled at the oldest joke once more：1978 年九月的菜单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 微笑（动名词 smiling at the oldest joke once more 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 露出（smile his thanks without words：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去露出不出声地把谢意写在脸上）
G. v. 露出（smile his thanks without words：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 微笑（后段两处：新来的客人照例 smiles his thanks without words，而母亲又一次 smiled at the oldest joke once more）

answers.why: smile 意为“微笑”，1984 年厨子小心翼翼地微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑，那是食堂里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 smiled。
smile 意为“微笑”，自那以后厨子当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 smiles。
smile 意为“微笑”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑”，此处为不定式 to smile at the oldest joke once more。
smile 意为“微笑”，菜单里 九月 那行字说明早在 1991 年之前就有人微笑过，故用过去完成时 had smiled。
smile 意为“微笑”，厨子说“微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 smiling at the oldest joke once more 作主语。
smile 意为“露出”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去露出不出声地把谢意写在脸上”，should ever 之后用原形 smile his thanks without words。
smile 意为“露出”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻露出不出声地把谢意写在脸上（smile his thanks without words at once），以后再也不要提起。
smile 意为“微笑”，新来的客人每个日子都照例露出不出声地把谢意写在脸上，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 smiles。
smile 意为“微笑”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑，用一般过去式 smiled 叙述。
smile 意为“微笑”，结尾那句是母亲 1996 年的话：要微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和食堂记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用

items: 1984 年，厨子小心翼翼地微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑；食堂里每一个客人都说这是头一回。（smiled at the oldest joke once more）
多年以后，厨子仍当天就做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（smiles at the oldest joke once more）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑这件事本身。（to smile at the oldest joke once more）
早在 1978 年就有人微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑，九月那天菜单上的一行字就是证据。（had smiled at the oldest joke once more）
厨子说过，小心翼翼地微笑又为那个老笑话微微一笑这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（smiling at the oldest joke once more 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻露出不出声地把谢意写在脸上，以后再也不要提起。（smile his thanks without words，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 smile 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1984 the cook smiled at the oldest joke once more with great care, and nobody in the canteen forgot it.
Even now the cook smiles at the oldest joke once more on the same day whenever the canteen asks.
Smiling at the oldest joke once more with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever smile his thanks without words on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new guest from the next canteen smiles his thanks without words with great care every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother smiled at the oldest joke once more again, and the canteen remembered that half.
